purpose: Defines the 20 single-pass streaming accumulators and telemetry analytics engine for computing behavioral, economic, and operational metrics across agent transcripts in O(N) linear time.
scope: Covers crates/lumen-analysis: RawMessageAccumulator and EntryAccumulator traits, 20 accumulators (token_usage, circuit_breaker, mcp_affinity, flow, turn_duration, tool_inventory, context_growth, permission_mode, hook_activity, api_health, pr_link, fuzzy_tools, attribution, self_correction, autonomy, schema_extractor, stats, timeline, artifacts, trajectory_dag), and subagent attribution. otel_correlation and span_mapping were removed in the 2026-08-20 real-data correction pass: otel_conversation_id (see api_surface) is now a plain field on CanonicalTranscript read directly rather than warranting a dedicated accumulator, and SpanMappingAccumulator was found to duplicate the pre-existing call_id field once compared directly against the real OTel semantic-conventions-genai registry.
non_goals: Log file format parsing or I/O streaming (handled by lumen-session).
Tarjan SCC cycle graph algorithms (handled by lumen-pattern).
Writing to disk or external databases (pure computation engine).

Genuine Draft-07 JSON Schema payload validation in SchemaExtractorAccumulator -- deferred pending resolution of where the 5 known schemas (spec@1, plan@1, changeset@1, eval-report@1, finding-report@1) should live relative to this repo, and creation of the still-nonexistent eval-report@1 schema.

Arena-based string interning or other zero-copy accumulation architecture to eliminate the inherent BTreeMap/BTreeSet/Vec ownership allocations in artifacts.rs, tool_inventory.rs, fuzzy_tools.rs, attribution.rs, and trajectory_dag.rs -- these are necessary to build deduplicated/aggregated output at all, not avoidable waste, and eliminating them is a substantially larger architectural investment than this spec contemplated.

GitLab merge_requests URL recognition in PrLinkAccumulator (CRIT-LUMEN-141) -- github.com/pull/{digits} is the complete v1 known-hosts pattern; GitLab support is a real, deferred gap, not silently absent.

Full output-struct/finalize()/edge-case specification for TurnDurationAccumulator (CRIT-LUMEN-064), ApiHealthAccumulator (065), McpAffinityAccumulator (066), and SelfCorrectionAccumulator (067) -- each currently has exactly one terse update-time criterion with no finalize criterion or zero-denominator edge case, unlike the richer pattern established for ContextGrowthAccumulator/FlowAccumulator. Pre-existing gap, not introduced by this pass; flagged for a dedicated follow-up (audit finding, 2026-08-20).

api_surface.name: RawMessageAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub trait RawMessageAccumulator { type Output: Serialize + Send; fn update_raw(&mut self, message: &serde_json::Value); fn finalize(self) -> Self::Output; }
api_surface.description: Lifecycle contract for single-pass stream accumulators operating on raw JSON frames.
error_conditions: Must handle missing keys without panicking

api_surface.name: EntryAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub trait EntryAccumulator { type Output: Serialize + Send; fn update(&mut self, entry: &CanonicalTurn); fn finalize(self) -> Self::Output; }
api_surface.description: Lifecycle contract for single-pass stream accumulators operating on semantic CanonicalTurn structs.

api_surface.name: TokenUsageAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub struct TokenUsageAccumulator { pub input_tokens: u64, pub output_tokens: u64, pub cache_creation_tokens: u64, pub cache_read_tokens: u64, pub per_model: BTreeMap<CompactString, ModelTokenSummary>, pub turns: u64 }; impl TokenUsageAccumulator { pub fn update_raw(&mut self, message: &serde_json::Value); pub fn finalize(self) -> TokenEconomics; }
api_surface.description: Single-pass token accountant tracking ephemeral 5m/1h cache writes, cache reads, and exact USD costs.

api_surface.name: PermissionModeAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub struct PermissionMetrics { pub auto_accepted_actions: usize, pub manual_approval_prompts: usize, pub auto_accept_rate: f32 }; pub struct PermissionModeAccumulator { pub auto_accepted_actions: usize, pub manual_approval_prompts: usize }; impl EntryAccumulator for PermissionModeAccumulator { type Output = PermissionMetrics; fn update(&mut self, entry: &CanonicalTurn); fn finalize(self) -> PermissionMetrics; }
api_surface.description: Approximates a session's autonomy-vs-manual-gating balance from turn-level signal alone (no real per-orchestrator permission-mode event exists in transcript data, per this session's HookActivityAccumulator findings -- this is a coarser, best-effort heuristic, not a claim of reading a real permission-system event). Was implemented (crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/permission_mode.rs) and counted in this spec's accumulator total but had zero acceptance criteria anywhere in this file until this fix (audit finding, 2026-08-20).
error_conditions: auto_accept_rate defaults to 1.0 when auto_accepted_actions + manual_approval_prompts == 0 (see CRIT-LUMEN-172)

api_surface.name: CircuitBreakerAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub struct CircuitStallEvent { pub agent_pair: CompactString, pub observed_rounds: usize, pub turn_index: usize }; pub struct CircuitBreakerReport { pub max_observed_rounds: usize, pub stalls: Vec<CircuitStallEvent>, pub tripped: bool }; pub struct CircuitBreakerAccumulator { pub max_observed_rounds: usize, pub stalls: Vec<CircuitStallEvent> }; impl CircuitBreakerAccumulator { pub fn update(&mut self, entry: &CanonicalTurn); pub fn finalize(self) -> CircuitBreakerReport; pub fn analyze_transcript(transcript: &CanonicalTranscript) -> CircuitBreakerReport; }
api_surface.description: Tracks multi-agent consensus iterations (e.g. Drafter and Auditor) and detects review stalls exceeding 2 rounds. CircuitStallEvent carries turn_index (real field, confirmed via crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/circuit_breaker.rs) identifying WHERE in its own transcript the stall occurred -- when a stall is merged up from a subagent transcript during recursion, that turn_index is relative to the subagent's own turns, not the parent's, since CircuitStallEvent carries no separate subagent/session identifier; distinguishing which subagent a merged stall came from requires cross-referencing the CircuitBreakerReport's own recursion structure, not the event itself. analyze_transcript recurses into CanonicalTranscript.subagents (which already models an arbitrary-depth tree via parent_session_id, crates/lumen-model/src/transcript.rs:14,20) so that stalls occurring across real subagent hierarchies are detected, not just within one flat turn list -- mirrors the recursion pattern CRIT-LUMEN-149 already establishes for AttributionAccumulator.

api_surface.name: SchemaExtractorAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub enum SchemaValidationResult { Valid, Invalid, UnrecognizedSchema }; pub trait SchemaValidator: Send + Sync { fn schema_id(&self) -> &str; fn validate(&self, payload: &serde_json::Value) -> bool; } pub struct SchemaExtractorAccumulator { pub validators: Vec<Box<dyn SchemaValidator>>, pub extracted: Vec<SchemaCitation> }; impl SchemaExtractorAccumulator { pub fn update(&mut self, entry: &CanonicalTurn); pub fn finalize(self) -> Vec<SchemaCitation>; } pub struct SchemaCitation { pub schema_id: CompactString, pub turn_index: usize, pub result: SchemaValidationResult }
api_surface.description: Generic $schema/$id-driven extraction with a pluggable per-schema-ID validator registry, tri-state result (Valid/Invalid/UnrecognizedSchema) instead of a boolean. Detection is generic (any embedded JSON block carrying a $schema or $id key), not hardcoded to Lumen's own 5 known schema IDs -- other plugin ecosystems will use different schema formats entirely, so the extraction layer must not assume any specific ecosystem's vocabulary. Validators register per schema_id; a schema ID with no registered validator yields UnrecognizedSchema (not Invalid -- absence of a validator is not evidence of a malformed payload).
error_conditions: UnrecognizedSchema when no SchemaValidator is registered for the extracted schema_id -- distinct from Invalid, which requires a registered validator that actually rejected the payload

api_surface.name: AttributionSource / CanonicalTurn.attribution
api_surface.signature: pub enum AttributionSource { Root, Plugin { name: CompactString }, Skill { name: CompactString, plugin: Option<CompactString> }, Agent { name: CompactString } }  // new field: CanonicalTurn.attribution: Option<AttributionSource>
api_surface.description: Tags each canonical turn with its originating plugin/skill (or Root), populated by adapters from Skill tool-call names or plugin-scoped tool namespaces, so AttributionAccumulator can key token spend by source (CRIT-LUMEN-147, 148). Plugin/Skill remain correct and unchanged for Lumen's own plugin ecosystem (confirmed by the user directly: our own plugins/skills/MCPs do have this predictable, structured shape). The new Agent variant is the ecosystem-agnostic fallback for orchestrators with no Lumen-plugin concept at all -- sourced from the real gen_ai.agent.name/gen_ai.workflow.name OTel attributes (verified directly against the real semantic-conventions-genai registry) -- so an orchestrator whose attribution shape genuinely differs from Lumen's own plugins gets a real, non-fabricated source instead of being forced into Plugin/Skill or silently dropped to Root.
error_conditions: Adapters that cannot determine any origin (neither a Lumen plugin/skill match nor a gen_ai.agent.name/workflow.name value) MUST leave attribution as None; AttributionAccumulator treats None the same as Root (unattributed_tokens), never fabricating a Plugin/Skill/Agent name.

api_surface.name: CanonicalTranscript.otel_conversation_id
api_surface.signature: pub otel_conversation_id: Option<CompactString>  // replaces the removed otel_request_ids: SmallVec<[CompactString; 2]>
api_surface.description: The session's real, native conversation/thread identifier (Claude Code's requestId, Codex's thread_id, Antigravity's conversation-id-as-directory-name), populated at parse time by the lumen-session adapter from a source-native field -- singular, matching the real OTel gen_ai.conversation.id attribute's actual per-session cardinality (verified directly against github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai's model/gen-ai/registry.yaml), not a collected list. Replaces both otel_request_ids (wrong shape -- a session has one conversation id, not a small accumulated list) and, together with CanonicalToolCall/CanonicalToolResult.call_id, the removed otel_span_id/SpanMappingAccumulator (redundant -- the real gen_ai.tool.call.id attribute is functionally identical to Lumen's pre-existing call_id field, confirmed by direct comparison against the same registry; no new correlation mechanism was needed).
error_conditions: MUST be None when the source has no native conversation/thread id available -- per the real registry's own explicit rule, a fallback UUID, trace id, or content hash SHALL NOT be synthesized as a substitute.

api_surface.name: HookActivityAccumulator
api_surface.signature: pub struct HookActivityAccumulator { pub hook_invocations: usize, pub by_event: BTreeMap<CompactString, usize>, pub total_duration_ms: u64, pub blocked_count: usize }; impl HookActivityAccumulator { pub fn update_from_hook_event(&mut self, event: &HookExecutionEvent); pub fn finalize(self) -> Self; } pub struct HookExecutionEvent { pub hook_event_type: CompactString, pub duration_ms: u64, pub blocked: bool }
api_surface.description: Tracks lifecycle hook execution counts by event name, cumulative duration, and permission-block rate from a dedicated hook-event source (an OTel execute_hook span, or an adapter-native hook event such as OpenHands' HookExecutionEvent), not from scanning message JSON for hookEventName -- confirmed this session, via a real 2894-line Claude Code transcript containing zero genuine hookEventName-shaped records, that hook telemetry does not live embedded in transcript text.
error_conditions: Where no hook-event source is available for a given orchestrator (mapping not yet confirmed for Codex/OpenCode/Antigravity), HookActivityAccumulator SHALL report all-zero counts rather than fabricating activity from transcript text.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN processing a session stream, THE SYSTEM SHALL execute the 18 EntryAccumulator-based accumulators in a single linear pass over the parsed turns in O(N) time. Heap allocation in the inner loop SHALL be minimized and reviewed statically per accumulator, not verified via a custom global allocator: this workspace sets unsafe_code = "forbid" (Cargo.toml), and implementing Rust's GlobalAlloc trait requires an unsafe impl block, making a runtime allocation-counting harness structurally impossible to build here. token_usage and hook_activity are exempt by design: both are RawMessageAccumulators operating on raw pre-parse JSON messages, invoked independently of AnalyticsEngine::process_transcript, not inside its per-turn loop.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Originally worded as requiring an empirically-measured zero-heap-allocation guarantee. A static audit (2026-08-20, during TASK-ANALYSIS-003) found 6 apparent violations. On closer engineering review, these split into two genuinely different categories: (1) AVOIDABLE, now fixed: circuit_breaker.rs called format!("parent->{agent_type}") on every SubagentSpawn call, allocating a throwaway String before wrapping it in CompactString -- replaced with direct construction via CompactString::const_new("parent->") + std::fmt::Write, which uses CompactString's own inline buffer when the result fits (compact_str 0.8 supports fmt::Write directly). pr_link.rs's unconditional per-turn BTreeMap::collect() was similarly found and fixed earlier in the same pass. (2) INHERENT, not a defect: artifacts.rs, tool_inventory.rs, fuzzy_tools.rs, attribution.rs, and trajectory_dag.rs each clone CompactString data into an owned BTreeMap/BTreeSet/Vec that must outlive the borrowed per-turn CanonicalTurn data and persist until finalize() -- this is the necessary cost of building any deduplicated or aggregated accumulator output at all, not wasted work. Eliminating these would require a fundamentally different architecture (e.g. arena-based string interning), which is a substantially larger investment than this criterion contemplated and is not undertaken here. Audit finding (2026-08-20): count corrected 19 -> 18 (this pass removed SpanMappingAccumulator, one of the 19 EntryAccumulator-based accumulators, dropping the real count by one -- the criterion's number was left stale) and the dangling otel_correlation per-turn-loop exemption clause was deleted, since OtelCorrelationAccumulator no longer exists as an accumulator at all (CRIT-LUMEN-152 is now a plain field-copy, not a pass-participating component -- there is nothing left to exempt).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN TokenUsageAccumulator processes an assistant message with usage, THE SYSTEM SHALL add input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, and cache_read_input_tokens to running totals.

WHEN CircuitBreakerAccumulator::analyze_transcript detects consecutive review handoffs between the same agent pair within a single CanonicalTranscript's turns, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment the round counter and flag a CircuitStallEvent if rounds exceed 2; WHEN transcript.subagents is non-empty, THE SYSTEM SHALL recurse analyze_transcript into each subagent CanonicalTranscript, APPEND every subagent's stalls onto the overall CircuitBreakerReport.stalls (a flat concatenation, not deduplicated or reordered), and set the merged report's max_observed_rounds to the MAXIMUM of the parent transcript's own max_observed_rounds and every recursed subagent's max_observed_rounds (not a sum) -- so a single deeply-stuck subagent is visible in the top-level max even if the parent transcript itself never stalled.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The recursion requirement is new this pass: confirmed structurally necessary three independent ways (Langfuse's self-referencing parent_observation_id, OpenHands' parent_id event tree, ccusage's real is_sidechain field plus sibling subagent files, all researched 2026-08-20). The fix connects to IR structure that already exists (CanonicalTranscript.subagents, crates/lumen-model/src/transcript.rs:20) rather than inventing new fields, and mirrors the recursion pattern CRIT-LUMEN-149 already establishes for AttributionAccumulator. Audit finding (2026-08-20): the original wording specified merging 'stalls' but was silent on max_observed_rounds -- now explicit (max-across-levels, not sum), and CircuitStallEvent/CircuitBreakerReport's real fields are now defined in api_surface so an implementer can see turn_index is relative to whichever transcript level produced it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN SchemaExtractorAccumulator scans a turn's entry.text field (the only field scanned -- tool_results.truncated_output is out of scope this pass, matching pre-amendment behavior) for an embedded JSON block carrying a $schema or $id key (generic detection, not hardcoded to Lumen's own 5 known schema IDs), THE SYSTEM SHALL record a SchemaCitation with result=Valid when a SchemaValidator is registered for that schema_id and it accepts the payload, result=Invalid when a validator is registered and rejects the payload, and result=UnrecognizedSchema when no validator is registered for that schema_id.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Generalized per the user's own direct clarification mid-session: Lumen's own plugin schemas ARE authoritative and predictable (registered validators can exist for them), but OTHER plugin ecosystems will use different, unpredictable schema formats -- a hardcoded is_valid boolean checked only against 5 known IDs cannot represent 'I don't recognize this schema' distinctly from 'I recognize it and it's wrong'. Design validated by Langfuse's real OtelIngestionProcessor/ObservationTypeMapper, an independently-built priority-ordered mapper registry solving the identical heterogeneous-producer problem. Real Draft-07 validation for Lumen's own 5 schema IDs remains a separate follow-up (still blocked on the cross-repo schema dependency question, per the prior wording's own reasoning) -- this pass changes the extraction/result SHAPE to be generic and pluggable, not the validation depth for any one schema. Audit finding (2026-08-20): the criterion didn't state which CanonicalTurn field(s) get scanned -- clarified as entry.text only, matching pre-amendment scope.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN TurnDurationAccumulator processes message timestamps, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute p50, p95, and average turn latency across all assistant completions.
WHEN ApiHealthAccumulator encounters a 429 rate limit or 5xx server error, THE SYSTEM SHALL record the error code, retry count, and retry latency in milliseconds.
WHEN McpAffinityAccumulator audits tool invocations, THE SYSTEM SHALL calculate the ratio of structured MCP queries versus fallback raw shell commands.
WHEN SelfCorrectionAccumulator observes a tool failure followed immediately by an adjusted parameter retry, THE SYSTEM SHALL record a tool_retry self-correction event.
IF a transcript contains synthetic model strings (starting with <synthetic>), THE SYSTEM SHALL silently exclude them from ModelTokenSummary billing.
WHEN subagent transcripts are processed, THE SYSTEM SHALL aggregate token spend by subagent role and compute the hierarchical economics breakdown.

WHEN ArtifactsAccumulator processes a turn's tool_calls, THE SYSTEM SHALL insert non-empty FileRead paths into files_read, non-empty FileCreate paths into files_created, and non-empty FileEdit paths into files_edited, while silently skipping empty-path variants and all other ToolIntent variants.

WHEN ArtifactsAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute total_unique_files as the size of the deduplicated union of files_read, files_created, and files_edited, such that a path present in more than one category set is counted exactly once even though it remains present in each of its category sets.

WHEN AutonomyAccumulator processes turns, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment current_streak and assistant_turns and update max_streak on TurnRole::Assistant or TurnRole::ToolResult, SHALL flush a non-zero current_streak into streak_lengths and reset it to 0 on TurnRole::User, and SHALL leave the streak neither extended nor broken on TurnRole::System.

WHEN AutonomyAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL first flush any still-open trailing streak into streak_lengths, THEN set max_autonomous_streak to the maximum streak length, avg_autonomous_streak to the mean of streak_lengths (0.0 if none), total_streaks to the count of flushed streaks, and autonomy_index to assistant_turns divided by total_turns computed over all roles including System (0.0 when total_turns is 0).

WHEN ContextGrowthAccumulator processes turns, THE SYSTEM SHALL skip any turn where entry.usage is None entirely, excluding it from turn_count, and SHALL set initial_prompt_tokens exactly once, from the first turn where usage is present.

IF a usage-bearing turn's prompt_tokens does not exceed the previous usage turn's prompt_tokens, or previous_prompt_tokens is 0 (the first usage turn processed), THE SYSTEM SHALL count zero growth for that turn toward total_growth and max_jump_tokens rather than a negative or default jump value.
WHEN ContextGrowthAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute avg_growth_per_turn as total_growth divided by (turn_count - 1), or 0.0 when turn_count <= 1.

WHEN StatsAccumulator processes a turn, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment total_turns by 1 and increment exactly one of user_turns, assistant_turns, tool_result_turns, or system_turns based on entry.role, mutually exclusive of the others.

WHEN StatsAccumulator processes a turn with entry.text = Some(text), THE SYSTEM SHALL add text.len() (UTF-8 byte length, not character count) to total_text_characters, and SHALL add nothing to total_text_characters when entry.text is None.

WHEN ToolInventoryAccumulator processes a turn's tool_calls, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment invocations_by_tool[call.tool_name] for every call and overwrite last_tool_name with each call's tool_name in list order, such that after a turn containing multiple calls, last_tool_name reflects the last call in that turn.

IF a turn's tool_results contains an entry with is_error = true, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment errors_by_tool keyed by the accumulator's running last_tool_name rather than any per-result tool identifier; IF last_tool_name is None at that point, THE SYSTEM SHALL drop the error without incrementing any counter.

WHEN FlowAccumulator processes a turn whose tool_results contain an entry with is_error = true and an error_class that case-insensitively contains "permission", THE SYSTEM SHALL flush a non-zero current_streak into streak_lengths, increment permission_blocks, reset current_streak to 0, and exclude that turn's tool_calls from the streak count; OTHERWISE THE SYSTEM SHALL add tool_calls.len() to current_streak.

WHEN FlowAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL flush any open trailing streak, set longest_streak to the maximum entry in streak_lengths, avg_streak_len to their mean, and flow_ratio to the sum of streak_lengths of at least 2 divided by the total tool_calls observed across the session.

WHEN HookActivityAccumulator.update_from_hook_event receives a HookExecutionEvent sourced from a dedicated hook-event stream (an OTel execute_hook span, or an adapter-native hook event such as OpenHands' HookExecutionEvent) rather than scanned from transcript message JSON, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment hook_invocations and by_event[event.hook_event_type], and SHALL add event.duration_ms to total_duration_ms.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The prior wording (scanning message["hookEventName"] out of transcript JSON) was confirmed this session to match zero genuine records in a real 2894-line Claude Code transcript -- every substring match was this very conversation's own text discussing hooks as a research topic, not an actual hook-execution record. Confirmed two independent ways (VS Code/Copilot's real OTel execute_hook span, OpenHands' native HookExecutionEvent type) that hook telemetry is a separate event/span stream, never embedded in transcript message text -- this criterion now targets that real source instead.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IF a HookExecutionEvent has event.blocked == true, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment blocked_count; WHEN HookActivityAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute block_rate = blocked_count/hook_invocations and avg_duration_ms = total_duration_ms/hook_invocations when hook_invocations > 0, and SHALL report 0.0 for both when hook_invocations is 0 (including when no hook-event source was available for the session's orchestrator at all).

WHEN PrLinkAccumulator scans a turn's VersionControl-paired tool_results.truncated_output and entry.text for a substring matching the form "{host}/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{digits}" where {host} is drawn from the known-hosts list -- github.com ONLY in this pass, a deliberately narrow v1 list, not an unspecified larger one -- THE SYSTEM SHALL split the matched path on "/" to bind {owner} and {repo} (owner and repo MUST NOT themselves contain "/"), discard any trailing path/query/fragment after the digit run, store the string "{owner}/{repo}#{digits}" in the deduplicated pr_urls set, and record the turn_index of the first such match in first_pr_turn_index.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Generalized from a github.com-only hardcoded match, which silently could never recognize any other host, to an explicitly-named known-hosts list. Audit finding (2026-08-20): the prior wording claimed GitLab was "a documented non_goal" when no such non_goals entry actually existed anywhere in the file, and "at minimum" left the known-hosts list's actual v1 contents ambiguous (github-only vs. some larger unstated list). Both fixed: the criterion now states plainly that github.com is the complete v1 list, and a real non_goals entry is added below deferring GitLab merge_requests support -- the gitlab.com/merge_requests URL form is removed from this criterion's pattern entirely rather than half-specified.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN a PR URL match's source is a tool_result whose paired tool_call is ToolIntent::VersionControl, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment linked_via_vcs_tool; WHEN a PR URL match's source is only entry.text, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT increment linked_via_vcs_tool.

WHEN FuzzyToolsAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL sort counts' keys (the BTreeMap<CompactString, usize> populated during the update phase per CRIT-LUMEN-154) by (-count, name), greedily assign each unassigned name as a new cluster's canonical, and assign a remaining unassigned name as that cluster's variant if and only if 0 < levenshtein(canonical, candidate) <= threshold, where threshold is 1 when candidate.len() < 5 and 2 otherwise.

WHEN FuzzyToolsAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute typo_call_count as the sum of all variant counts across all clusters, and typo_rate as typo_call_count divided by total_tool_calls (0.0 when total_tool_calls is 0).

WHEN TrajectoryDagAccumulator processes a tool_call, THE SYSTEM SHALL set target_file/target_symbol from ToolIntent::{FileRead,FileEdit,FileCreate}.path (target_symbol = None) or ToolIntent::CodeSearch.query (target_symbol = query, target_file = None), and SHALL set is_mutation = true for FileEdit, FileCreate, or VersionControl with action "commit" or "push", and false for all other intents. For FileDiscovery, TestExecution, SubagentSpawn, McpCall, Other, and VersionControl with any action other than "commit"/"push", THE SYSTEM SHALL set target_file = None, target_symbol = None, and is_mutation = false.

IF a tool_call has no tool_result with a matching call_id in the same turn, THE SYSTEM SHALL default had_error to false for that ToolNode; WHEN a matching tool_result exists in the same turn, THE SYSTEM SHALL set had_error to that result's is_error value.

WHEN AttributionAccumulator processes a turn whose attribution is Some(AttributionSource::Plugin{name}) or Some(AttributionSource::Skill{name,..}), THE SYSTEM SHALL add that turn's total token usage to by_plugin[name] or by_skill[name] respectively; WHEN attribution is Some(AttributionSource::Agent{name}), THE SYSTEM SHALL add it to by_agent[name] (a new BTreeMap<CompactString, u64> field, distinct from by_plugin/by_skill since an Agent-sourced turn has no Lumen plugin/skill concept to key on). by_agent is keyed by an AttributionSource-derived, OTel gen_ai.agent.name/workflow.name value and is a DIFFERENT axis from CRIT-LUMEN-149's by_subagent, which is keyed by transcript-tree position (CanonicalTranscript.subagents nesting) -- a turn can be Agent-attributed within a subagent transcript, contributing to both maps simultaneously; the two are not mutually exclusive or redundant.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Extended to cover the new AttributionSource::Agent variant (gen_ai.agent.name/workflow.name-sourced), the ecosystem-agnostic fallback added this pass for orchestrators with no Lumen-plugin concept. Audit finding (2026-08-20): by_agent's similarity to the pre-existing by_subagent (CRIT-149) risked being read as redundant or overlapping -- clarified as two genuinely different, independent axes (attribution-source-type vs. transcript-tree-position).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IF a turn's attribution is None or Some(AttributionSource::Root), THE SYSTEM SHALL add its token usage to unattributed_tokens rather than to by_plugin or by_skill.

WHEN the analysis engine processes a CanonicalTranscript with a non-empty subagents field, THE SYSTEM SHALL recurse AttributionAccumulator (or an equivalent token roll-up) into each subagent transcript and aggregate its token totals into by_subagent, keyed by that subagent CanonicalTranscript's own subagent_role field (SPEC-LUMEN-001-MODEL, populated at parse time per SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION's CRIT-LUMEN-026 -- the real <worker> filename segment, not an invented identifier); a subagent transcript with subagent_role == None (should not occur via the CRIT-LUMEN-026 path, but not structurally impossible) is keyed under a literal "unknown" bucket rather than silently dropped or panicking. Requires process_transcript to recurse into subagents where it currently does not.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-20): "subagent role" was referenced with no defined source anywhere -- CanonicalTranscript had no role field at all. Closed by adding CanonicalTranscript.subagent_role (SPEC-LUMEN-001-MODEL, populated by SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION's CRIT-LUMEN-026 from the real, already-confirmed <worker> sibling-filename convention) rather than inventing a call_id-based correlation with no evidence it's available in real data.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN TimelineAccumulator processes turns, THE SYSTEM SHALL extend an open streak counter while consecutive turns have role == Assistant, and on any turn with a different role SHALL close the streak, increment assistant_streak_count, and update longest_streak_turns to the maximum streak length observed so far.

WHEN TimelineAccumulator processes a turn and last_timestamp is Some(prev) with (current_timestamp - prev) exceeding 5 minutes, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment idle_gap_count, add the gap to total_idle_ms, and update longest_idle_gap_ms if the gap is the largest seen; THE SYSTEM SHALL always update last_timestamp to the current turn's timestamp regardless of gap size.

WHEN an AnalysisReport is finalized from a CanonicalTranscript, THE SYSTEM SHALL copy transcript.otel_conversation_id through into the report unchanged, without any dedicated accumulator pass -- the reduction from many real per-API-call requestId values (or equivalent per-orchestrator native IDs) down to this one singular field happens entirely at parse time, inside the lumen-session adapter (SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION's CRIT-LUMEN-164, which states the full first-non-sidechain-wins precedence rule); by the time the analysis layer sees CanonicalTranscript, that reduction is already complete, so no FURTHER aggregation happens at THIS layer.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: OtelCorrelationAccumulator is removed this pass, not merely rewritten: once otel_request_ids (a collected list needing aggregation) became otel_conversation_id (a singular already-set field), no accumulation work remained to justify a dedicated accumulator -- a plain field copy is the whole job. This criterion's ID is retained in place per this repo's rewrite-not-renumber convention, now describing the field-copy behavior that replaced the removed accumulator's finalize() logic.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN FuzzyToolsAccumulator (an EntryAccumulator) processes a turn's tool_calls, THE SYSTEM SHALL increment counts[call.tool_name] (a BTreeMap<CompactString, usize>) for each call and add tool_calls.len() to total_tool_calls.

WHEN PermissionModeAccumulator processes a turn with role == TurnRole::User whose text, after trimming whitespace, is exactly "y", "yes", "ok", or "proceed" (case-sensitive exact match, not a substring/contains check), THE SYSTEM SHALL increment manual_approval_prompts by 1; WHEN processing a turn with any role OTHER than User that has a non-empty tool_calls, THE SYSTEM SHALL add tool_calls.len() (not 1) to auto_accepted_actions. A User turn whose text does not match one of those four exact strings, or has no text, increments neither counter.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: PermissionModeAccumulator was implemented (crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/permission_mode.rs) and counted in this spec's accumulator total but had zero acceptance criteria until this fix (audit finding, 2026-08-20). Bound directly to the real, already-implemented update() logic, verified by direct code read.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN PermissionModeAccumulator finalizes, THE SYSTEM SHALL compute auto_accept_rate = auto_accepted_actions / (auto_accepted_actions + manual_approval_prompts); IF that denominator is 0 (no permission-relevant signal observed in the session at all), THE SYSTEM SHALL return auto_accept_rate = 1.0, matching the real implementation's default, rather than 0.0 or NaN.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: The zero-denominator default (1.0, i.e. treating a session with no observed permission signal as fully autonomous) is an explicit judgment call being made and recorded here, not silently inherited from the code without comment -- a total of 0 could equally be read as 'no data, undefined' rather than '100% autonomous.' Matches the real implementation's existing behavior (permission_mode.rs:37) rather than changing it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FIXED 2026-08-23. WHEN a caller needs CanonicalTranscript.detected_anomalies populated for a real transcript, THE SYSTEM SHALL provide lumen_analysis::detect_trajectory_anomalies(&CanonicalTranscript) -> SmallVec<[TrajectoryAnomaly; 4]>, covering TrajectoryAnomaly::CircularLoop (via lumen_pattern::detect_circular_loops, Tarjan SCC over the transcript's own tool-call graph) and TrajectoryAnomaly::GateStall (via CircuitBreakerAccumulator, already wired into AnalyticsEngine's per-turn pass but never reachable from any caller). lumen-cli's load_sessions SHALL call this for the root transcript and every subagent transitively, each scoped to its own turns (not flattened across the tree), before any command persists or displays a transcript.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Full-codebase semantic-model review finding (2026-08-23): detected_anomalies was hard-coded empty by every adapter (no adapter can detect a cross-turn pattern while streaming one line at a time -- this is inherently a post-processing step, not adapter work), and CLI-facing has_anomalies was therefore always false. But 2 of TrajectoryAnomaly's 4 variants turned out to already have real, tested, unreachable detectors: lumen_pattern::TrajectoryGraph::detect_circular_loops (the exact Tarjan SCC feature README's Comparative Matrix already advertised) and lumen-analysis's CircuitBreakerAccumulator (CircuitStallEvent{agent_pair, observed_rounds} is an exact field match for GateStall). Root cause: lumen-cli had zero dependency on lumen-analysis or lumen-pattern at all, traced to the same refactor this session's memory already flagged (CLI rebuilt around lumen-store, old commands using these crates removed, the detectors themselves never deleted, just orphaned). User explicitly chose to wire both real detectors now and explicitly chose to defer the other two variants: ContextFlood needs a real flood-threshold judgment call this criterion does not make (partial data exists via ContextGrowthAccumulator, but no detection logic), and UngroundedDrafting has no supporting detector or accumulator at all -- both left as documented, deliberately deferred gaps rather than guessed at. has_anomalies is now real when persisted, but SessionSummaryReadModel/SessionDetailReadModel in lumen-store still don't carry it back out, so `lumen sessions`/`lumen session` cannot yet display it -- a separate, smaller follow-up, not addressed here. Regression tests: crates/lumen-analysis/tests/test_anomalies.rs (4 tests, both kinds individually and together, and a true-negative case) and crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs's load_session_populates_detected_anomalies_from_a_real_circular_loop (end-to-end through the real CLI fingerprint -> parse -> detect path).
